# Digitakt II: agent context pack

Data checked 2026-11-28, research snapshot `85e9e1256aad`. Generated from the Aggregat database; every item links back to the Markdown that is the source of truth. Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. Evidence: `[hw]` seen on a real unit, `[emu]` emulator only, `[doc]` stated without a test result, `[?]` unclear or inferred.

Full version. The brief one is [digitakt-2-brief.md](digitakt-2-brief.md).

## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc] [hw]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [emu] [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]
- **A79** Test every edit path on a pattern, bank and project far from the defaults, not only on A01. [hw]
- **A80** A parameter a mod sets right before it plays a note may be smoothed by the OS: set the smoothing state too, or set the value a few blocks earlier, and listen on a unit. [hw]
- **A81** A sound a mod starts without a trig must obey the track's mute itself. [?]
- **A82** On the Octatrack, read the Part a track is playing from stock's per-track pair (`0x8000182a` / `0x80001832` + t), not from the UI or engine Part. [hw]
- **A83** Test the smallest legal build as well as the full one. [hw]
- **A84** When you patch a stock routine for audio tracks, find its MIDI-track twin and patch and test that too. [hw]
- **A85** A mod machine that stock sees as another machine must handle both edges of a machine switch itself. [hw]
- **A86** Take key ids from the target device's own decoder table, never from another model. [emu] [hw]
- **A87** Place card data by the smallest capacity the firmware accepts, and check the capacity the driver reports before you touch the card. [hw]
- **A88** When a mod changes the USB descriptors at run time, bring the controller back from a context that keeps running, check that it attached, and keep every other host client off the device while it reconnects. [hw]
- **A89** On the Octatrack, do not change which effects the DSP holds while a project loads; plan only from the complete effect map. [hw]
- **A90** Load from the card only when a sound needs it, never on every knob or modulation step. [hw]
- **A91** Rewrite a playing track only behind the playhead, and expect the change on the next loop. [emu] [hw]
- **A92** Before you bring a dormant stock routine or buffer into use, find what else uses that memory. [doc]
- **A93** A USB Audio layout must run on the host's own class driver before you ship it. [hw]
- **A94** Do not gate a feature on a one-time handshake sent at link-up; re-detect the peer from ongoing traffic. [doc]
- **A95** Data a saved pattern or project points to must not change after the save; act on a stock reload only once the stock has accepted it. [hw]
- **A96** Check every precondition of a RAM boot before anything is uploaded, and count every restart against a pending update. [hw]
- **A97** Keep a stock UI widget inside the range stock gives it. [hw]
- **A98** Draw only from the task that owns the screen; from a tick or a higher-priority task, post a request instead. [hw]
- **A99** When you add rows, questions or pages to stock UI, redraw them yourself and use stock's own windows for questions. [hw]

## 2. Rules that name the Digitakt II

- **C1** (C) One mod = one OS version. Addresses and stock bytes are version-specific (hash-pinned). A mod for Digitakt mk1 1.53 is refused on 1.54; Digitakt II 1.17 addresses do not carry to 1.18+. Porting = find every address again. Keep a separate build per OS version. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting} {digitakt2-perform}
- **C10** (C) Calibrate the emulator against stock and the unit before trusting its numbers. Call stock routines in the emulator and compare with what they must return (complex-ping's check found that its SHARC emulator shifted every fractional multiply); measure one timing per project on the unit and carry the ratio (2x on the DT2 for DDR-reading code, 7-12x in one digimod case, a hard stop that overshot 3x as far). An emulator that agrees with itself proves nothing about silicon. The display is part of this: digikit's emulator showed intro frames upright that the panel showed upside down. Check one asymmetric picture on the unit before trusting the emulator's orientation. Pointers too: a Digitakt II UI pointer that digikit's emulator filled stayed 0 on the unit; find screens from what the OS drew, not from UI object pointers ([I106](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i106-a-ui-pointer-the-emulator-filled-stayed-0-on-a-digitakt-ii)). Incidents: [I36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i36-the-emulator-undercounted-dsp-time-by-2x-to-12x), [I37](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i37-a-sharc-emulator-shifted-every-fractional-multiply), [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel). `[hw]` {own-dt2-notes} {digimod} {dn2-skill-md} The same holds for event fields: Modwerk read a knob's own push-button byte as FUNC, and an emulator reference screen lacked markers the unit draws. Incidents: [I55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i55-a-knobs-own-push-button-byte-was-read-as-func), [I56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i56-a-test-plan-pressed-the-wrong-key-and-the-emulator-reference-did-not-match-the-unit). State an emulator's cost per emulated second (instruction budget divided by instructions per second), not per run: trig-seedr read 5 emulated seconds as one and overstated an idle cost five times ([I128](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i128-idle-cpu-cost-overstated-five-times-an-instruction-budget-read-as-one-second-trig-seedr-analog-emu)).
- **C12** (C) Before you blame your mod, check [STOCK-BUGS.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/STOCK-BUGS.md) and reproduce the misbehaviour on the unmodified OS with the same steps; a stock bug you find goes into that list. The reverse holds too: before you call it a stock fault, check that your own watchdog does not mistake one of stock's deliberate pauses for a fault - Modwerk's Octatrack base read the DSP pause of USB DISK MODE as a stall ([I69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i69-a-mod-took-stocks-usb-disk-mode-pause-for-a-dsp-stall-and-kept-the-audio-off)). Mods reach stock paths, and stock paths have bugs: a Part change by a mod shows the Octatrack's carry-over bug exactly as a stock pattern change does, and a damaged project halts stock and modded Digitone II builds alike. Record a new stock bug with the device and OS, the trigger, the cause if known and how it was found, and your workaround. Incidents: [I2](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i2-stock-song-load-trusts-a-stored-row-count). `[hw]` {dn2-oldproject} {kyoti-bugfixes} A test failure right after a restart can be stock's boot too: in digikit's emulator the Digitakt II dropped stock MidiRpc requests while its boot intro ran, which failed a storage test (not yet checked on a unit); wait for the firmware's own ready state before the first request ([I114](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i114-stock-midirpc-requests-were-lost-while-the-boot-intro-still-ran)).
- **D10** (D) Disclose AI-generated code the way DT-FM does ("largely AI-generated, not proofread"). Not a technical rule, but readers decide on risk from it. `[doc]` {dt-fm} D10b. Device-specific core rules (elekloader ADAPTING.md, 2026-10): Digitakt II has no render events (audio runs on the DSP) - subscribe only `.run` code to `ev_key`/`ev_enc` before the first tick; Digitone II has no `.fast` code (such mods are refused), remote panel input uses `core_keys_set`/`core_keys_clear`, SysEx uses `ev_sysex`, SHARC mods run at the master output in 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz with a 428-byte stack; RAM budgets: Digitakt mk1 128 KB (256 KB with core 4.0) plus 2,304 B fast SRAM, Analog Rytm MKII 128 KB and no fast SRAM; Digitone mk1 core 4.1.1 changed SETTINGS-row allocation (before it two rows could stall a first boot); each feature needs a minimum core version in `resources.core`. `[doc]` {elekloader-adapting}
- **D13** (D) Keep a trap register in your agent file. Known entries: OLED y runs bottom-to-top (`63 - y`; elekloader `ev_draw`: y=0 is the bottom row); on DT2/DN2 the stock intro's bitmap uses another layout than the main-UI blit (pixel (x, y) at byte `8*x + (63-y)/8`, bit `7 - (63-y)%8`, measured on a DT2; [I53](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i53-boot-screen-frames-were-upright-in-the-emulator-and-flipped-on-the-panel)) {digikit-f117}; compile ColdFire code with `-fno-ipa-sra` when using `-O2` (reported to corrupt interrupt pointers); `-mcpu=5475 -Os` is what the Digitone II skill uses; no libc (zero-initialised locals become `memset`); on the Octatrack `0x80000012` (MIDI tracks shown) is a long, so a byte read always gives 0 ([I123](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i123-a-byte-read-of-a-long-flag-hid-the-midi-tracks)). Add each new surprise when you meet it. `[?]` {dubspot} {dn2-skill-coldfire} A software-started ColdFire eDMA channel runs one minor loop unless it is linked to itself (ELINK), as stock's channel 47 is ([I197](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i197-an-edma-block-without-a-self-link-moved-only-its-first-16-bytes-synfact-stereo-tracks-syntakt)). {synfact-1123}

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [hw] Test your DIN interface before you need it. On a DT2, a generic "USB2.0-MIDI" cable adapter (VID 1a86, PID 752d) delivered nothing, while a controller's DIN out worked. Cheap cable adapters are known to drop or mangle long SysEx; a stock-OS dry run with your exact cable is the only proof. `[hw]` {dt2-lab-coldfire-fix} ([I44](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i44-recovery-used-on-a-digitakt-ii-after-a-crashing-build-a-cheap-cable-delivered-nothing)) (`recovery#73f47f95`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L20))
- [doc] Digitakt II OS 1.16 is no longer on Elektron's download page (author suggests asking Elektron support). Keep stock files you may need. `[doc]` {digitakt-ii-research} (`recovery#5a9efa40`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:25](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L25))
- [doc] Two upgrade paths: from within the OS (Transfer, DROP page, confirm with YES on the device; devices whose OS does not fully support Transfer are sent to the LEGACY OS UPGRADE page) and from the Startup Menu (device's MIDI port, not USB; hold FUNC while powering on; TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; Transfer in LEGACY OS UPGRADE mode). `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#67684a45`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L28))
- [doc] "Some upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap" right after the first restart; do not turn the power off then. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#065677fb`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L29))
- [doc] Downgrading is not supported and is at the user's own risk; user content may be lost. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#258d6d79`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L30))
- [doc] Digitakt II, first reboot after upgrading to OS 1.15: a file-system integrity check (up to a minute). On errors: back up all projects and samples with Transfer, SETTINGS > SYSTEM > FORMAT +DRIVE (tick SAMPLES), re-import. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} (`recovery#00f8aff4`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L31))
- [doc] Heat +FX: in-OS path is SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with the file sent through MIDI In or USB MIDI In; the startup path takes MIDI In only. `[doc]` {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#2a7bab5e`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L32))
- [doc] Digitakt II (digitakt-ii-research `RECOVERY.md`): keep an official stock `.syx`, a physical MIDI interface and cable ready; MIDI OUT of the interface to the Digitakt II's MIDI IN (USB MIDI cannot be used); hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; in Elektron Transfer open the SYSEX TRANSFER page and choose "OS upgrade via device startup menu"; select the stock file and keep power on until the unit reboots. No durations are given and the author states recovery is not guaranteed if the startup menu or bootloader cannot run, power is lost during a critical write, or storage/hardware is damaged; the page reports no hardware test of the procedure. `[doc]` {dt2-recovery} (`recovery#2c2f6817`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L35))
- [doc] Digitakt II: hold FUNC while powering on, press the key the startup menu shows; project slot 001 is overwritten with the factory project and the loaded project is cleared; sound/preset bank A is overwritten; other slots/banks untouched; samples on the +Drive are kept. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-support} (`recovery#40019018`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:62](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L62))

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB20** Each USB controller reset leaks a timer slot (DT2/DN2, static reading) (Digitakt II OS 1.17, Digitone II OS 1.12; open, unconfirmed). Workaround: do not call the reset path repeatedly from a mod.
- **SB35** A Data API card write takes its length from the host and is bounded only by the card's end (Syntakt, OS 1.42 (the same eMMC write and erase code is in Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.11/1.12; whether their Data API sizes a write the same way is not read); open in stock). Workaround: a host client must bound the size to the slot; digikit's card guard hooks both entries and refuses a request outside the stock area `[0, 0x180000)` (emulator-tested).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I70** A 1024-byte bulk IN transfer wedged the Digitone II's USB controller. Cause: the controller has a 64-byte transmit buffer per endpoint. Two back-to-back 512-byte IN packets wedged it the moment the host read them; OUT with two 512-byte packets was fine. Stock does the same thing on purpose: it declares its MIDI IN endpoint as bulk 512 but programs the queue head for 64-byte packets (caps `0x20400000`), as in its audio and Overbridge modes. A first guess (dTD page pointers) was not the cause. Fix: the bulk IN queue head is programmed for 64-byte packets while the descriptor keeps 512; the host reads short packets until a frame is complete. Echo then matched from 1 byte to 1 MiB at about 2.3 MB/s each way (DN2) and 2.9 MB/s (DT2), and the emulator now faults an IN transfer whose packets after the first exceed 64 bytes. Rules: A39.
- **I114** Stock MidiRpc requests were lost while the boot intro still ran. Cause: digikit's runtime answered at once after the restart, but the firmware was still on its boot intro, which drops stock MidiRpc requests. A boot race, not storage code. Fix: after `restart()` the host's first stock RPC waits for the stock service with a read-only probe (up to about 30 s); a write is never resent. digikit's debug log now has event 47 FW_READY, written with the block counter on the first UI-loop pass after boot; hosts wait on it before they send stock MidiRpc requests (2026-11-18, {digikit-1118}). Rules: C12.
- **I14** DAG registers stored through their own DAG hung the DSP. Cause: `DM(I7, M7) = M4` and similar; the PRM forbids it and stock never does it. Fix: move DAG registers through an R register. Rules: A33.
- **I15** A frequency shifter froze the unit at boot. Cause: a selas defect left a nested hardware-loop end compressed; code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. Fix: `.NOCOMPRESS` around nested loops; cache write-back before running copied code. Ran on send and master 2026-10-30. Rules: A45,A28,A41.
- **I16** A decoded section 7 over 1 MiB crashed the unit. Cause: the ColdFire depacks section 7 into a 1 MiB buffer and checks the size only afterwards. Fix: keep the decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes. Rules: A46.
- **I17** Per-sample stores to the DDR output buffer crashed the unit. Cause: per-sample accesses to stock buffers in external DDR (`0x8045b3c0`). Fix: render into L2 and copy once per block. Rules: A52.
- **I18** The flash cave reportedly froze a unit at the logo. Cause: not settled ([CONFLICTS O18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/CONFLICTS.md)). Fix: check the bytes the other cave users leave; prove the cave on a hard run. Rules: A43.
- **I23** Plaits builds failed normal Transfer updates at PREPARING. Cause: not stated; the author says not to assume the route is reliable everywhere. Fix: power cycle and the startup menu. Rules: A20,A36.
- **I27** An encoding every decoder accepts raised ILOPI on the chip. Cause: negative shift immediates with zero sign bits in the middle parcel (stock: `023e 7800`); selas's 48-bit `Rn = <sysreg>` put the wrong register (EMUCLK read as LCNTR). Fix: stock encodings only; compressed forms for system registers; check the disassembly. Rules: A41,G9.
- **I80** A USB mode take-over left a Digitakt II off the bus until a power cycle. Cause: the stock mode switch stops the controller with no lock; most likely the detach never reached the line (the controller stopped while the external ULPI PHY was suspended or busy), or the PHY was left in a state the stock restart does not undo. The stock firmware writes no PHY register itself. Fix: digikit holds the restart for 2 s, parks the PHY's line (function control through ULPI_VIEWPORT) while the controller is stopped and spaces switches at least 3.5 s apart. That made the failure rarer, not absent, so the take-over is off by default since 2026-11-13; with USB CONFIG set to USB MIDI (no switch) the fast transfer was fully reliable. Rules: A55.
- **I93** A recorder mod's startup reservation blocked project load and save on a Digitakt II. Cause: the buffer setup at startup set the reservation ownership flag even with no audio, and both project entry guards refuse while it is set. Fix: a candidate that leaves the buffer keys out of the pool during save, rebuilds empty reservations after load, and lets stock's recovery save to slot 128 through. Rules: C9.
- **I94** An OS 1.17 rebuild of a recorder mod hid its buffers in a project saved with its OS 1.16 version. Cause: the 1.16 version can leave identity markers in sample rows H124-H127; R1 needs them empty and hides the buffers when the reservation fails. Fix: none yet; use a new project. Rules: C9,E3.
- **I147** Kit data overlapped the project archive: a module setting came back off after a power cycle (Modwerk). Cause: core 1.1's kit data (191 B) ran into the last 48 B of the kit record that the base's project archive uses; saving a kit-data module zeroed the archive. Fix: base `8650bb8a` ends core's kit data before the archive (`KIT_ROOM` 146, one byte of the package); a check refuses an overlap. Rules: A78.
- **I150** Powering off on a mod page broke the stock Euclidean page at the next boot (Euclidean Scale). Cause: at startup the stock Euclidean view's track-editor cache is unset; the module read the track from that cache. Fix: read the track through the stock Euclidean view's own accessor (S117); confirmed on the unit. Rules: A40.
- **I36** The emulator undercounted DSP time by 2x to 12x. Cause: the emulators model no memory stalls. Fix: budget with silicon costs; leave a margin; measure once per project on the unit. Rules: A35,C4,C10.
- **I41** A label defined twice resolved to the wrong file. Cause: a label defined in two sources resolves to one of them in the merged object. Fix: unique label prefixes per file. Rules: D4.
- **I53** Boot-screen frames were upright in the emulator and flipped on the panel. Cause: the emulator decodes the intro bitmap as if the intro flush flipped like the main-UI blit. On the panel, intro rows are stored top-down mirrored. Why the intro path differs (flush routine or panel scan direction) is not established. Fix: digikit's `.dkbs` frames, safe screen and pixel helper use the panel's layout. The emulator decoder is not fixed yet. Rules: C10,D13.
- **I61** Odd jump targets froze a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator kept running. Cause: byte-aligned code sections put routines at odd addresses; a jsr/jmp to an odd address stops the ColdFire with an address error (vector 3), while the emulator keeps running. Fix: the linker refuses an odd-target absolute jsr/jmp into mod RAM; each code section starts with a 2-byte alignment. Rules: A42.
- **I67** Code built into .bss crashed a Digitakt II at boot; the emulator ran the zeros. Cause: two new routines were placed in `.bss` instead of the code section, so the unit jumped into zero-filled memory. The emulator executed the zeros as no-ops and booted. Fix: the routines are code again in 2.6.1. The README says not to flash a 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6 build; Digi2MacroOSC and Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM still name core 2.4. Rules: A42,C10.
- **I106** A UI pointer the emulator filled stayed 0 on a Digitakt II. Cause: the module found the mixer through the view controller's page-set pointer at `+0x9c`, which was non-zero in the emulator and 0 on the unit. Fix: 0.1.3 recognises the mixer from the frame the OS has just drawn; about 2 h on the unit with core 1.0. Rules: C10.
- **I44** Recovery used on a Digitakt II after a crashing build; a cheap cable delivered nothing. Cause: the cable. Fix: rehearse recovery with your exact cable and the stock file. Rules: A11,A36.
- **I54** Safe mode by REC at power-on, tested on a Digitakt II. Cause: test. In the emulator, digikit's earlier queue scan missed the key (`safe:0`); reading the stock key state fixed it. On the unit, a key held at power-on does produce a report. Fix: — Rules: A29.
- **I237** A conditional SHARC return froze a Digitakt II (Modwerk assembler, Morpha). Cause: Modwerk's own SHARC assembler encoded `IF cond RTS` in a form the chip handled correctly only when the return was taken. Fix: the plain form, checked in the emulator; FOLD then passed on the unit with base 948be0c4. Rules: A41.

## 6. Open conflicts (sources disagree)

- **O20** DT2/DN2 stock intro frame rate: A) 30 Hz: digikit's PIT3 model (PCSR `0x093f`, PMR 8593), so the first scene table's 175 frames last 5.8 s (finding 117) B) 15 Hz: digikit's earlier emulator notes derive it from divisor 1024 (66.67 ms per frame; finding 07)
- **O18** DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` at boot: A) unusable: "digikit's flash_cave (0x403117c4) froze the device at the logo: that trailing region is not loaded or is cleared on the hardware, whatever the emulator does" (a comment in dt2-capicola's build script, vendored in dt2-machine-lab) B) usable: Deja Vu's releases put their payload there and were validated on a unit for boot and operation; 70b185's builds put a stub there and run on a unit; digikit's canary survived boot in its emulator
- **O7** Free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17: A) static: free up to `0x200fa000` (digikit finding 100) B) the owner's unit: clicks and delay leaks past `0x200f5a74`
- **O8** DT2/DN2 NOR flash geometry: A) bootstrap: 512-byte pages, 256 KB erase B) in-OS writer: 0x100-byte pages, 0x10000 sectors from `0x80000`
- **O24** Digitakt II NRPN numbers (OS 1.17): A) the OS 1.17 manual: track mute 1:101, track level 1:100, pattern mute 1:104, master overdrive 2:37, filter env depth 1:23, filter base/width 1:51/1:52, portamento 3:7/3:8 B) midi.guide's data: 1:108, 1:110, 1:109, 2:50, 1:26, 1:24/1:25, 3:6/3:7 (the mute and level numbers match the Digitone II's)
- **O25** Digitakt II LED colour byte (OS 1.17): A) digikit finding 19: the byte is a colour mask B) digikit finding 122: on a unit `0x31` shows deep blue and `0x41` yellow (one observer, by eye)
- **O27** DT2/DN2 FX slots a module runtime offers: A) 4 FX slots (our [`common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md), from earlier digikit docs) B) 3 FX slots on both devices (digikit `docs/plans/runtime-and-services.md`, 2026-11-15); digikit also gives DN2 send slots as 1 there and 0 "for now" in its upload design
- **O29** CRC of a block in stock's 0x51 OS upgrade write: A) common/os-update-protocol.md (DT2/DN2): zlib `crc32(data)` B) Modwerk LINK.md (Analog Rytm MKII): zlib crc32 seeded with 0xffffffff {modwerk-rytm-link}
- **O34** Syntakt OS container cap: A) Modwerk: at most 2 MB (the upgrade's receive buffer) {modwerk-st-goal} B) digikit `syntakt.toml`: `container_max = 0x300000`, copied from DT2/DN2 with the Syntakt flash map not read; digikit's own finding 141 puts the analog calibration record at NOR `0x300000` (backup `0x340000`), so a container from `0x80000` longer than `0x280000` would reach it {digikit-st-1118}
- **O37** Digitone II parameter row: MIDI fields at +0x18..+0x24 (OS 1.12): A) dn2-cfw: `+0x18` MIDI CC, `+0x1c` NRPN, `+0x20` Overbridge id {dn2-cfw-param-table} B) digikit (checked against the image by a second reader): CC and NRPN are both halfwords at `+0x18`, `+0x1c` is the slot, `+0x20`/`+0x24` are template words; same layout on the DT2 {digikit-1119}
- **O39** Digitakt II wire parameter `0xea` (OS 1.17): A) digitakt-2.md (2026-11-19, from findings 148-149): `0xea` is the filter type's wire parameter, and an incoming CC or NRPN for it is dropped {digikit-1119} B) digikit finding 150: `0xea` is parameter row 6 "Machine Type"; the machine setter and the filter setter both send it, and the receiving side was not examined {digikit-1120}

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H2** (stock) Unsaved edits survive a power cycle on the DT2 and the DT1 as on the DN2, because the stock edit writer stores each edit in the sound record at once. Test: On a throwaway project, turn a filter knob, do not save, power-cycle. Is the value still there? Also try a parameter lock.
- **H3** (stock) A received pattern dump lands in the slot armed on the unit, not in the slot its index byte names (shown on the DN2 by syxgrid). Test: On a throwaway project, send a pattern dump with index A05 while A02 is armed, using Elektroid or digi-roll. Where does it land?
- **H5** (stock) Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01). Test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?
- **H19** (stock) The stock start-up animation runs at 30 frames per second, so it lasts about 5.8 s (175 frames), not about 11.7 s at 15 fps (O20). Test: Film a cold start with your phone, three times, and time the animation from its first frame to its last; also say whether it looked the same each time (one of five animations is picked at random, the first about 99.9 % of the time).
- **H24** (stock) The Digitakt II and Digitone II hang on LOAD TO PROJECT of a +Drive file that is not a sample, as the Analog Rytm MKII does (SB19), since their sample browsers list every file too. Test: Back up first. On a throwaway project, put a small non-audio file on the +Drive with Elektroid, LOAD TO PROJECT, note what happens; then power-cycle, delete the file and run CREATE NEW before the next OS update.
- **H25** (stock) The Digitakt II on OS 1.17 answers midi.guide's NRPN numbers (track mute 1:108, track level 1:110, pattern mute 1:109, master overdrive 2:50), not the manual's (1:101, 1:100, 1:104, 2:37) (O24). Test: On a throwaway project, send each NRPN pair from a DAW or a MIDI tool on the auto channel with value 0 and then 127, and watch which parameter moves on the screen.
- **H27** (stock) A Digitakt II or Digitone II drops stock MidiRpc / Transfer requests while its boot intro still plays, and answers them once the main screen is up (digikit's emulator, 2026-11-16; I114). Test: Power on with Elektron Transfer (or another MidiRpc tool) connected and start a file listing as soon as USB appears; note whether the request fails or hangs during the intro and works after it.
- **H37** (stock) The Digitakt II's stock USB MIDI transmit path (OS 1.17) waits indefinitely for buffer space when the host stops reading. Test: Send a SysEx request whose reply is large, keep the port open but stop reading, and watch whether the UI and sequencer keep running.
- **H54** (stock) On a stock Digitakt II (OS 1.17), changing a track's filter type sends the same MIDI parameter as a machine change (`0xea`, the "Machine Type" row, or (`0xf`, type) in the other send mode), because the stock filter setter `0x40051886` is a copy of the machine setter `0x40051712` (O39). What a receiving unit does with it is unknown. Test: Stock OS, MIDI out (CC/NRPN) to a computer MIDI monitor: change the filter type on the FLTR page, then the machine; compare the messages. Optionally send the captured message into a second unit and see what changes.
- **H55** (stock) A stock project rename on a Digitakt II or Digitone II keeps the save stamp (32-bit word at slot record +`0x18`), so a tool keyed on the stamp follows a renamed project. The rename callback (DT2 `0x400a1246`, DN2 `0x4009b3bc`) does not call the stamp builder directly; what its change notice triggers is not traced. Partly answered 2026-11-21: in the DN2 1.12 emulator a menu rename of the *current* project gave it a new live stamp, written at the next save; a non-current slot keeps its stamp by static reading. `[emu]` Test: Read the slot listing (with a tool that reads it) before and after a rename in PROJECT MANAGER; compare the stamp.
- **H6** (probe) The DT2's SHARC DDR above the sample pool window (`0x9d22b9c8` up to `0xa0000000`, about 46 MB) is never written by stock, as the DN2's tail `0x80531000-0xa0000000` is not. Test: dnfw's method: fill the range with a pattern at boot, then scan it during heavy playback, pattern and kit changes, FX extremes, sample loads and a save. Expect a reserved top part for Capicola builds only.
- **H7** (probe) The DT2's ColdFire runs the same FreeRTOS layout as the DN2: higher priority numbers run first, prio 0 never runs, prio 1 is the idle loop; the main task's stack is barely used. Test: With the USB probe: find the ready table and the running-task pointer, sample them 60 times.
- **H9** (probe) The DT2 flash cave `0x403117c4-0x40312000` is safe on a stock image; the freeze report (O18) came from something else in that build. Test: A stock image plus a canary in the cave, read back after a cold start after a long power-off (A40).
- **H28** (probe) On a project load, `write_live_project` (DT2 `0x400df95a`) and `fx_array.load` (`0x400daf54`) run in the project-load task (stack `0x4039beac` + `0x4000`), not in the UI task (stack `0x4096775c` + `0x28000`); finding 135 shows reachability only. Test: PC probe at those addresses logging A7 and SR while a project loads; A7 in the first range = project task.
- **H14** (build) The SHARC's IIR0/FIR0 accelerators compute on the DT2 exactly as measured on the DN2 (output from stored word 5, FIR sums in pairs, INIDX/OUTIDX written the other way round). Test: Port the accelprobe image to the DT2 and compare the 76 result words.
- **T3** (needs unit + a USB mod, effort M) Test rule A39 (no EP0 stage of a multiple of 64 bytes) on a small box with a vendor request. The DT2 has the same EHCI-style controller with EP0 max packet 64 and its own EP0 vendor requests (digikit 42), so it is the best candidate
- **T7** (needs unit + custom engine, effort L) Find the cause of the sticky "bitcrush until reboot"
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)
- **T14** (needs unit + emulator, effort M) Fix or document digikit's EMAC fractional-mode emulation against a unit measurement
- **T15** (needs unit, effort M) Probe free SHARC L2 on DT2 1.17 between `0x200f5a74` and `0x200fa000` on a unit
- **T18** (needs files, effort M) Document the project file formats (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`) beyond song slots

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

## 9. All 458 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] 1 GHz core (20 MHz x 100 / 2), 32-sample blocks at 48 kHz = 1,500 blocks/s = 666,667 cycles/block. This is confirmed on a real DT2 by the owner's idle counter. `[hw]` — `dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain#4593dacc` [hardware/common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md:39](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md#L39) · Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Time and DSP link
- [doc] [emu] [hw] digikit's planning budget (2026-11-14): a selection must fit 85 % of the 666,667-cycle block after the stock baseline, with emulator instruction counts projected to cycles by a high factor: that leaves 194,244 instructions per block on the DT2 and 92,796 on the DN2 (12,140 and 5,799 per voice at 16 voices). These are planning instructions, not the cycles measured free on a unit, so do not compare them with the `[hw]` headroom figures directly. On DN2 1.12 the whole DSP ran 332,039 instructions per block in the emulator with one note playing (stock baseline 334,529); the DT2 stock baseline is about 211,000. `[doc]` / `[emu]` {digikit-budget} — `dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain#94b90e88` [hardware/common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md:43](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-limits-and-audio-chain.md#L43) · Digitakt II / Digitone II - firmware limits, DSP calling convention and the audio chain (DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12) / 3. Measured median per block: DT2 666,582, DN2 666,784 (digikit); DN2 666,706 (elekloader's idle-task meter); the owner's idle counter on a DT2 agrees. {digikit-f103} {elekloader-sharc-dn2} {own-dt2-notes} — `dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck#e9d9674c` [hardware/common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md:8](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/dt2-dn2-sharc-crosscheck.md#L8) · Digitakt II and Digitone II SHARC: which findings hold on both (task T19, 2026-11-02) / 1. - [doc] [hw] Section 7 must stay under 1 MiB, stored and decoded (DT2 and DN2). At boot the ColdFire allocates two `0x100000`-byte buffers, copies the stored section into the first, writes a `0x03` byte at the start of the second and depacks the section after it. The decoded-size check (`len + 1 > 0x100000`, status 3) runs after depacking (DT2 1.16 `0x400cd20c`; the same 828-byte routine on DT2 1.17, DN2 1.11 and 1.12) {digikit-f06} {digikit-f01}. So an oversized stream is not refused cleanly: it overruns the buffer first. A dt2-machine-lab build with a 1,314,460-byte decoded stream hit a ColdFire exception on a unit and was withdrawn; the lab's repair encodes zero regions as fill blocks so the decoded stream fits {dt2-lab-capicola}. elekloader states the same limits for the DN2 ([`../devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitone-2-machines-sampler-sharc.md)). Count decoded bytes with a depacker, not the stored size (rule A46). `[hw]` The earlier README named sections 3 and 7 as patch targets. `[doc]` {digikit} {digikit-old} — `firmware-container#0682353e` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:34](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L34) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Sections

- [doc] [hw] Maintenance mode (a power-on key combination, or a reboot marker) presents a USB CDC-ACM serial port, VID `0x1935` PID `0xFFFF`. It speaks a line protocol: `#COMMAND\n` text lines, `!` + 4-byte big-endian length for binary frames. About 60 factory commands. Read-only examples: `#HELLO` (answers "HOW DO YOU DO?"), `#STATUS` (reports `PLATFORM PCBA0109..`, `PRODUCT 52;5;15;Digitone II`), `#READ_SERIAL` (the "SERI" record at flash `0x3C0000`). Writing commands change persistent state: `#WRITE_SERIAL`, `#WRITE_TESTED`, `#WRITE_UI_TESTED`, `#WRITE_AUDIO_TESTED`, `#MMC_RECONFIGURE`, `#WRITE`, `#UPGRADE`, `#FULL_UPGRADE` (unchecked flash path, see `os-update-protocol.md`). Agents never send these. `[doc]` (digi-roll-studio's ceremony - copy it) 1. Re-read and back up the whole destination pattern first; abort if the backup fails. 2. The target's OS build must be on an allowlist. 3. The user confirms a dialog listing the changes. 4. Change only the bytes that must change. 5. Read the result back and byte-compare. Also: keep a local stash of overwritten patterns (50) plus pre-restore snapshots (10). `[hw]` {digi-roll-studio} — `sysex-and-midi#1d9d72a8` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:134](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L134) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Hardware ports and the hidden service console (DT2 1.16 / DN2 1.11)
- [hw] selache pitfalls that halt a real DSP but run in the emulator (elekloader ADAPTING.md, Nov 2026; the first matches 70b185's DT2 finding): A shift by a negative immediate (`LSHIFT R1 BY -16`) is encoded without sign extension. Put the count in a register (`R2 = -16; R1 = LSHIFT R1 BY R2;`). elekloader's lint flags candidates, but it cannot see instruction boundaries, so check each one in the listing. A C function whose locals sit more than ~63 words from the frame pointer is compiled wrongly. One large local array is enough. The manual allows them, but they are unproven on silicon. The shipping kernel does SIMD compute only and moves every load and store in SISD, toggling PEYEN per sample as stock does. - [hw] The stock engine governs its own per-block load. With 8 heavy stock tracks the Audio task ran at 99-100 % for whole 4 s windows and missed no block. Misses happen only when extra code inside the Audio task adds work the stock governor doesn't know about. - [hw] Provoked missed blocks (54 in one boot, three back to back) did NOT cause the sticky bitcrush. Neither did stock overload, nor sample loading at low load. The sticky "everything bitcrushed until reboot" appeared only with several custom-engine tracks at extreme settings. An emulator write audit showed no stray stores, so the cause is still open. - [hw] Which words are free (DT2 1.17, measured): 670-676 arrive untouched. heavylight's engine uses 672-676. Words 1-6 are rewritten by the firmware after the block, so writes there never arrive. Word 5 is the firmware's while a track plays (unlike the DN2). 677-686 are the firmware's. From word 7 on there is a per-track table: 21 words per track at `0x8000488C + 0x1C + 84*track`. `[hw]` — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#006943d0` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:36](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L36) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 4. - [hw] Knob frame working copy: short at `0x2558dc + 0xde + 0x60*track` (the hidden CFADE slot, 0..0x7f00). Routing a value through this "free" slot also feeds a stock per-voice flag that acts on the delay feedback (`FUN_1c24e9`, slot struct `0x2506ec + v*0xdc + 0x10`). - [emu] [hw] Samples go to the DSP over link port 0 (LP0_CTL `0x30FFE000`; SEC sources 81/82/168), not over the frame link. LP1 is unused. One transfer is 0x401 words: a tag and 1,024 payload words. Tag `0xFFFFFFFF` means a slot header: slot, startL, startR, rate, len. Stereo means startL != startR. A tag below `0x19200` is a page number into the 400 MiB DDR sample pool at `0x8422B9C8`. This is the RPC-task work the owner saw while samples load. — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#b5c49fef` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:46](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L46) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5b. - [hw] Read-only USB SysEx probe in MAIN OS (heavylight's dt2-keyframer, derived from irpina/digihealth via dn2_firmware_explore): `F0 00 20 3C 7D 00 <pack7> F7`. Commands: HELLO 1 (returns word 0) and PEEK 3 (address, up to 256 bytes). There is no write command. It hooks the SysEx router at `0x40120006` (router `0x4011ffda`, header `0x4021e5d2`, send `0x40121d2a`, USB port 2), and the router itself drops device id 0x7D. It fits in 532 bytes of a free 896-byte run in MAIN OS 1.17 (`0x402e4f64`, `0x402e609c`) and coexists with Deja Vu V5.1, Musical V4 and Zoom V11. It also went into an elekloader-built image. It is built with plain binutils (`m68k-linux-gnu-as -mcpu=5475`). - [hw] A second SHARC stop on a real DT2: `fx/freqshift` on the send route froze the unit at boot; the emulator showed nothing (findings 77, 91). Two causes were found. `[hw]` {digikit-f91} ([I15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/INCIDENTS.md#i15-a-frequency-shifter-froze-the-unit-at-boot)) A selas defect left the end of a nested hardware loop compressed (VISA). The last 11 instructions of every hardware loop must be 48-bit ISA, so wrap nested loops in `.NOCOMPRESS` ([rule A45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md)). Code copied into L2 at run time was not written back from the data cache. - [emu] UART8 receive is done by eDMA (channel 34), not by reading the data register - an emulator must model eDMA, not just the UART. `[emu]` {digikit-f08} — `memory-maps#a499b2b2` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:21](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L21) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [emu] Card pools inside the firmware area (MmcFs) `[emu]` {digikit-samples}: Fixed slots: projects 0-127 (16 MiB each on both), sounds 0-2047 (DT2 4 KiB, DN2 1 KiB), kits 0-1023 (DT2 64 KiB, DN2 32 KiB). The bitmaps at sector `0x800` are write-protect padlocks, not occupancy. The boot project (magic "COKi") has two copies at sectors `0x40000` and `0x48000`. The working project is at `0x50000` and is rewritten from the boot copy at every start. The DT2 has a path filesystem (ekFS +Drive) for samples. The DN2 has none: only the MmcFs pools. - [emu] Call: R4 = voice record (`0x2412cc + v*0x1d8`, 32 records), R8 = output (32 floats, 48 kHz, int16/32768 scale), R12 = 32. Voices are rendered in ascending order 0..31, so a new block starts when v <= last v. Record words: w00 sample pointer (int16 mono, L = voice 2t, R = 2t+1), w62/63 length, w64/65 loop start, w68/69 end (Q31), w6a/6b step (Q31, 96 kHz units), w6c/6d phase, bytes 0x1b8 active / 0x1b9 stop / 0x1bb reverse / 0x1bc loop, w72 = a (tempo fit, float) and w73 = b (pitch ratio). A trigger is visible as w70 == w71 == 0. +4 is a 96 kHz work buffer and +0x104 is decimator state, not scratch. Tempo is a float BPM at DM `0x252d50`. `[emu]` — `digitakt-2-sharc-measured#ef662e52` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-sharc-measured.md#L40) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - SHARC facts measured on a real unit / 5. WAVE 0-5 dispatch through a 6-entry table at `0x4022231c`; WAVE 6 is RAND. The table cannot be extended by appending: the RAND slew data sits right after it. The shared RNG is `(A,B) -> (B, A+B)` at `0x402b62c8/cc`. The phase increment is in D5 (signed); the stored phase is in D2. Raw WAVE 7/8 clamp to 6 and play RAND on stock. - [emu] Every ColdFire task switch passes through `vector_32_handler` at `0x40000410` (20,760 entries on DT2 and 17,778 on DN2 over the probe window). Vector 205 is the switch entered from an interrupt, always from stacked IPL 0; vector 32 (`trap #0`) is a task yielding, with SR 0x2700; vector 191 does not occur, and no switch is entered from a handler at IPL 2 or higher. - [doc] What is settled: Section 8 is a complete ARM Cortex-M firmware image: a Thumb vector table, and a descriptor naming a 1 MB flash window at `0x60000000` with the image at `0x60042000`. The same 159,948-byte image (sha256 `6943b2f2...`) ships in Digitakt mk1 1.53, Digitone II 1.11, Analog Rytm MKII 1.73 and Analog Four 1.55D. Syntakt and Digitakt II carry a section 8 of the same size. It is not an FPGA bitstream (the FPGA is section 1, or inside section 7 on the Digitone mk1), and it is not code for the device's own CPU. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} {analog-emu-a4} {rytm-fw-re} — `firmware-container#ded70082` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:61](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L61) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / Section 8: one shared ARM firmware image (merged from dnfw, analog-emu, digikit, rytm-fw-re)
- [doc] SysEx transport: each message is `F0 ... F7`; the body is either a 126-byte data packet or a 14-byte marker; it starts with the manufacturer ID and a device ID: DN2 `0x15`, DT2 `0x14`, DN1 `0x0D`. Payloads use 8-in-7 encoding (116 encoded bytes carry 101 decoded bytes, last packet zero-padded); packet count = stream length / 101 + 1 (an exact division still adds a packet); a block and sequence counter starts from values in the start marker and wraps at 7 bits; the 7-bit packet checksum sits in the last body byte and uses a base value taken from the start marker, not a constant. `[doc]` {dn2-ele3} — `firmware-container#aec8faff` [hardware/common/firmware-container.md:90](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md#L90) · Firmware container (.syx) - facts shared by the devices / ELE3 container in detail (dnfw `docs/ele3-format.md`, read 2026-10-31)
- [doc] CPU fingerprint: NXP MCF5441x (ColdFire V4m with EMAC) - UART8 `0xEC070000`, GPIO `0xEC094000`, eDMA `0xFC044000` (TCDs +0x1000), INTC0-2 `0xFC048000/0xFC04C000/0xFC050000`, DSPI0 `0xFC05C000`, PIT0-3 `0xFC080000-0xFC08C000`, EPORT `0xFC090000`. Stock Ghidra misdecodes EMAC line-A words; digikit uses a separate language spec. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} — `memory-maps#c63308d3` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L18) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] DDR is 128 MiB (DDRMC writes in the bootstrap; earlier 64 MiB claims are wrong): `0x40000000-0x47FFFFFF` cached (ACR0), `0x48000000-0x4FFFFFFF` an uncached alias of the same DDR used for DMA buffers; reset SP `0x48000000`; 32 MiB C++ heap above `0x44000000`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} — `memory-maps#ece09d6e` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:19](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L19) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [?] [doc] NOR flash 16 MiB, S25FL127S-class (RDID mfg 0x01, id 0x2018); the bootstrap's flash loop uses 512-byte pages and 256 KB erase blocks. The in-OS writer (finding 75) uses 0x100-byte pages and 0x10000 sectors from flash `0x80000` - two code paths, two geometries `[?]`. `[doc]` {digikit-f08} {digikit-f75} — `memory-maps#519a00ac` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:20](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L20) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] No ColdFire watchdog. Neither MAIN OS (DT2 1.16/1.17, DN2 1.11/1.12) nor the bootstrap names the core watchdog registers (CWCR `0xFC040016`, CWSR `0xFC04001B`), and the watchdog is off after reset. A ColdFire hang therefore stays hung until a power cycle; nothing resets the unit for you. Static reading; computed addresses are not excluded. Third-party MCF5441x code agrees that the core watchdog stays off after a power cycle unless software enables it, and CWCR can be written only once after reset (so a bootstrap write of 0 would also lock it off). `[doc]` {digikit-f17} {netburner-cwt} {nxp-mcf5441x-rm} — `memory-maps#40215568` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:22](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L22) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] eMMC part table: DT2 1.16 (`0x402b4a24`) and DN2 1.10E/1.11 (`0x4029f554`) accept the same seven 32-byte entries: Kingston parts `TX2932` and `TS0A32`, both 32 GB, matching the Kingston EMMC32G-TX29 on a DN2 board photo. Shared ColdFire storage code: the block driver, the MmcFs slot store and the transfer routing; the sample filesystem, its request handler and the sample manager are DT2-only. `[doc]` {dn2-drive} — `memory-maps#22432990` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:23](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L23) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)
- [doc] eMMC card (both, about 32 GB part, 0x2E1A000 sectors assumed): sectors `0x0-0x457FFF` belong to the firmware (boot, tables, projects, pools, presets); MmcFs refuses writes at `0x457FFF` and above. DT2 1.17: factory sample table "MaGj" at `0x458000` and 1,265 factory samples to `0x5D7FFF` - never touch; +Drive (ekFS) `0x5D8000-0x2DF017F`; `0x2DF0180` to the end unused. DN2 1.12: nothing stock writes at `0x458000` and up; FORMAT trims only up to `0x457FFF`. Unchecked bank ids in the Data API can reach every sector below `0x800000` over USB - put any private store above that line (digikit: DT2 `0x2DF1000+`, DN2 `0x800000+`). Not checked on a real card. `[doc]` {digikit-f59} — `memory-maps#501b88cc` [hardware/common/memory-maps.md:24](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/memory-maps.md#L24) · Memory maps and mod areas per device (from elekloader's `docs/DEVICES.md`, v0.9.0 era) / Platform facts from the firmware itself (Digitakt II / Digitone II, digikit finding 08 and 59)

- [doc] Modes -> descriptors: USB MIDI PID `0x012b` (EP1 bulk pair, 2 cables); USB AUDIO/MIDI PID `0x102b` (UAC2 iso on EP2/EP3 + MIDI on EP1); OVERBRIDGE PID `0x0b2b` (vendor class 0xFF: interrupt EP3 in/out, EP2 OUT bulk 512 + EP2 IN interrupt 64, plus MIDI on EP1); a service mode PID `0xffff` with CDC-ACM. - [doc] The type bytes differ, so never reuse a type table across devices: Rytm: dumps `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` pattern, `0x55` song, `0x56` settings, `0x57` global; `0x58-0x5D` the same objects from the unsaved work buffer; requests `0x62-0x6D` the same way. Digitakt / Digitakt II / Digitone II: `0x50` pattern plus kit in one message, `0x51` pattern, `0x52` kit, `0x53` sound, `0x54` project settings; requests `0x60-0x64`, and `0x6F` asks for the whole project. So `0x54` is a Rytm pattern but a DT2/DN2 project-settings message. syxgrid's guess "`0x53` = kit" for the DN2 (graded D, unknown) is a sound dump by digi-roll's table. `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} {syxgrid-map} — `sysex-and-midi#7642b2b0` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:35](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L35) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Device byte in dumps: Rytm (libanalogrytm's era, MKI) `0x07`; Digitakt `0x0A`; Digitakt II `0x14`; Digitone II `0x15`. A DN2 answered only `0x15` in a sweep and ignored `0x0B-0x0E`, `0x14` and `0x16`. The same bytes appear in the OS files ([`firmware-container.md`](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/firmware-container.md)). `[doc]` {libanalogrytm-sysex} {digi-roll-protocol} Three different device ids. They are easy to mix up, and the same number means different devices in different namespaces: — `sysex-and-midi#4c310635` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:40](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L40) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Elektroid reads the product id from byte 5 of the decoded `Device` (Ping) reply and looks it up in its device table; digi-roll captured 42 and 43 from a DT2 and a DN2 the same way. The FAQ table on elektron.se (Heat `000A`, Digitakt `000C`, Digitone `0014`, Heat MKII `0016`, Model:Samples `0019`, Model:Cycles `001B`, Digitone Keys `001C`) matches Elektroid's table entry for entry, so that table lists product ids. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {digi-roll-protocol} {elektron-faq} — `sysex-and-midi#a82f614a` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:55](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L55) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Elektroid's further product ids: Analog Four `0x04`, Analog Keys `0x06`, Analog Rytm `0x08`, Analog Four MKII `0x0E`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x10`, Syntakt `0x1E`. Overwitch's Overbridge ids: Analog Four MKII `0x0B47`, Analog Rytm MKII `0x0B48`, Digitone Keys `0x0B35`, Syntakt `0x0B4A`. digikit read the DT2's USB ids from the image: `0x012B` (USB MIDI), `0x102B` (audio/MIDI), `0x0B2B` (Overbridge), so the low byte is shared across modes. `[doc]` {elektroid-devices} {overwitch-devices} {digikit-f42} — `sysex-and-midi#5388b9cc` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L56) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Dump messages and device ids across generations (task T22, 2026-11-02)
- [doc] Unpacked request body: `seq_hi seq_lo 00 00 type payload...`. The two bytes after seq must be `00 00`. A non-zero byte there and the unit never replies. — `sysex-and-midi#26a2be46` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L81) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] Unpacked reply: `counter16 seq16 (type|0x80) payload...`. The first pair is a device-side counter, not the seq; the echoed seq is the second pair. — `sysex-and-midi#23194457` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:82](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L82) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The whole body is 8-in-7 packed, one collector per 7 bytes. Short bodies (Ping, `ReadDir /`) look unpacked, which misled early tools. Longer payloads must be packed or the unit answers "Invalid path". — `sysex-and-midi#9b9d3eba` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L83) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] All integers are big-endian, strings are NUL-terminated (< 256 bytes), and no checksum is used. — `sysex-and-midi#fe5d9257` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:84](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L84) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] No wire-controlled memory read or write exists over MidiRpc. Eight surfaces were audited (Data partial R/W, path resolvers, FsRaw, the backup streams, the route table, the full type factory). Live RAM is not reachable this way; the OS-upgrade path writes flash only. `[doc]` — `sysex-and-midi#869c11db` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:108](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L108) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The factory debug console is on UART8, not MIDI: `#HELLO`, `#READ`/`#WRITE` (an 11-name parameter table, not memory), `#DUMP_AUDIO`, `#ENTER_TEST_MODE`, `#MRAM_DUMP` (a fixed 13.8 MiB factory/calibration blob, magic "COKi"), `#MMCDUMP` (raw eMMC sectors). It is not known to be reachable from outside. Agents: leave it alone. `[doc]` — `sysex-and-midi#cdad2325` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:110](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L110) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The live Transfer protocol, MidiRpc (Digitakt II 1.16/1.17; digikit `docs/MIDI-SYSEX-RPC.md`) `[doc]`
- [doc] The same screen request works on more devices: Elek View, a browser port of screendump that sends the request in the `F0 00 20 3C 10 00` RPC framing, was tested on a Digitakt II and a Model:Cycles, and its author reports an Analog Heat MKII working too. So the Heat MKII speaks this RPC framing; whether the Heat +FX does is a stock test (HYPOTHESES H18). `[doc]` {elek-view} — `sysex-and-midi#bde6941b` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:118](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L118) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II specifics and client pitfalls (dnfw `midi-rpc.md`, live on a DN2 1.11)
- [doc] Project files (`.dt2prj`, `.dn2prj`, also Model:Samples/Cycles) are renamed zip files holding a compressed project image named after the project, a `manifest.json` and, on sampling devices, a samples folder. Decompress-recompress scripts round-tripped projects that then loaded on DN2, DT2, M:S and M:C (forum post, no log); the compression is LZ4 according to syxgrid's author. `[doc]` {em-dx2-scripts} — `sysex-and-midi#d0e282a7` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:119](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L119) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Digitone II specifics and client pitfalls (dnfw `midi-rpc.md`, live on a DN2 1.11)
- [doc] The panel MCU sends 2-byte packets on UART8: key packet: `0x20 | channel`, then the channel's 8-bit button mask; encoder packet: `0x30 | (encoder-1)`, then a signed 8-bit delta; high nibble 7: the factory console. — `sysex-and-midi#8472cf05` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:122](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L122) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Key code = `channel*8 + bit + 1` (codes 1-48, plus a few exceptions per device). There are nine encoders. — `sysex-and-midi#97f65e08` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:126](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L126) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Toward the panel: `B9 idx val` sets an LED to a palette entry, `B5 i r g b` sets a palette entry. — `sysex-and-midi#bcfe4cfd` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:127](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L127) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / The panel wire protocol (digikit finding 58, DT2 1.17 / DN2 1.12) `[doc]`
- [doc] Connectors: `system` (local computer, for format conversion), `elektron`, `cz`, `sds`, `efactor_preset`. Elektron filesystem families: raw/sample (`raw`, `preset-raw`, `sample`), data (`data`, `project`, `preset`, `preset-takt-ii`, `sound`), memory (`ram`, `track`). The Digitakt II "Preset" filesystem is implemented as `preset-takt-ii`. `raw` and `data` are for testing only and not compatible with Transfer formats. A firmware `upgrade` command exists in the CLI (which devices is not stated). Device definitions come from `~/.config/elektroid/elektron/devices.json` if present. Elektron samples cannot be swapped. `[doc]` {elektroid-readme} — `sysex-and-midi#dcc899c9` [hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md:165](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/sysex-and-midi.md#L165) · SysEx and MIDI control (talking to a unit without flashing it) / Elektroid (dagargo) - a general sample/SysEx client

- [doc] digikit (current home ElekLabs/digikit, `[doc]` {digikit}): native Rust emulator running ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together with front panel, display and audio; web panel (WASM) and Tauri desktop app; `patchkit` applies modules to the user's own `.syx` and refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8; headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes; control socket for patch injection; ColdFire/DSP analysis databases and Ghidra tooling. Targets: Digitakt II 1.17 (also runs 1.16; 1.15C for old analysis), Digitone II 1.12 (also runs 1.11; 1.10E for old analysis). Caveats: DSP not real-time yet; browser host parked on `wip/browser-host`; no patched firmware installed on a device by the author; bootstrap-menu recovery untested on hardware. AGPL-3.0-or-later with NOTICE terms asking for the credit "digikit by Em D". — `toolchain-and-emulators#936e3acb` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:50](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L50) · Toolchains and emulators / Emulators
- [doc] Earlier digikit README (m-dwyer/digikit, {digikit-old}) described a Python/Unicorn design: ColdFire emulator for Digitakt II / Digitone II; patched Unicorn m68k (SR read, CCR sync, EMAC MAC with load; stock Unicorn refused); ColdFire-aware disassembler because Capstone misses MVS/MVZ and FF1; first run needs a cold boot of a few minutes to build snapshots; about 10M instructions/s. Works: core, interrupt controllers, PIT, DMA timers, eDMA, front-panel TX, display, SD/MMC up to identification. Missing then: DSP (no audio), input path, block storage - partly superseded by the Rust version above. `[doc]` {digikit-old} — `toolchain-and-emulators#6a21af16` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L51) · Toolchains and emulators / Emulators
- [doc] Elektron Emu (xerydian): five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) running each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU - Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles; the user supplies the `.syx` in a per-machine folder; +Drive emulated and persisted, WAV loading on DT2/Rytm/DN2; Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler; otherwise a slow interpreter that renders offline only); limits: Rytm analog voices are a custom model that does not sound like the machine, Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; 2 commits, no licence stated. `[doc]` {elektron-emu} — `toolchain-and-emulators#d1f1bb43` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L81) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] Stock Unicorn 2.1.4 (and QEMU master as of 2026-09-15) gets ColdFire wrong in ways that change results (emu-elektron's patch notes) `[doc]` {emu-elektron-patches}: Condition codes: they are committed lazily, so a hook or a counted stop in mid-block sees stale flags, and the next branch goes the wrong way. MAC/MSAC with load is decoded wrongly in four ways: Ry with bit 0 or 1 set faults as "dual accumulate" on a CFV4E; Rx is always D2; MSAC adds instead of subtracting (this also hits MSAC without load); MASK is applied to every load address. The DT2 main OS reaches one of these at `0x400db9e0`. EMAC fractional and signed arithmetic is wrong (as found by SyntHack and octabam). EMAC saturation with MACSR.OMC gets its sign and constants wrong. Any ColdFire emulator built on Unicorn needs these fixes before its audio or branch results mean anything. emu-elektron carries all of them as patches for five devices. — `toolchain-and-emulators#f0b75153` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:83](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L83) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] Current Selache fork (pin 967c1d1e) build rules: a plain `.SECTION/DM` is laid out in 40-bit words, so digikit assembles DM data as `/DM/BW`; the assembler may set a DO loop's fast-loop F1 bit by itself, so turn that off and write `(F)` where it is meant; `Rn = Fm` is not a plain transfer, use `Rn = PASS Fm`; an undefined name (for example a register SHARC+ lacks) silently becomes an external symbol. The earlier assembler wrote 77 transfers without their width modifiers. `[doc]` {digikit-1116} — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#e2c02a74` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:51](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L51) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 4. - [doc] Three pieces of stock code: a vector stub, the wrapper `0x1c02a4`-`0x1c066b` (byte-identical on both images, 968 words, return label `0x1c04b7`; it calls the handler through the table at `0x2404b0` with `JUMP (M13, I12) (DB)` at `0x1c04b1`) and a return stub. SEC vector stub DT2 `0x1c0b7b` / DN2 `0x1c0acd`, generic stub `0x1c0b1e` / `0x1c0a70`, return stub `0x1c0be5` / `0x1c0b37`: the DN2 stubs sit `0xae` lower. `[doc]` (both images' bytes, two decoders) — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#751041dd` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:99](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L99) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] What is saved: the stubs save R4, R8, R12, I6, I7, I12, B6, B7, PX and PCSTK; the wrapper saves the DAG, status, loop-stack and MR/MS registers and zeroes L0-L5 and L8-L15 for the handler. It picks its path by MODE1 bit 16 (RND32) of the interrupted code: with RND32 set it saves only R0-R2, R4 and S0-S15 and relies on the handler to keep the C callee-saved registers; with RND32 clear it saves R1-R15. `[doc]` — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#7a5c301c` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:100](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L100) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. How a stock DSP interrupt saves registers, and what module code must never write (digikit findings 130, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12)
- [doc] Never write these in module DSP code, not even with a save and restore: B7, L6, L7, M5, M6, M7, M13, IMASK, IMASKP, IRPTL, MMASK, TPERIOD, TCOUNT, FLAGS. The stock interrupt code may read them at any instruction, so an interrupt between the save and the restore sees the changed value. The wrapper needs a valid linear stack in I7 (L6 = L7 = 0) and M5 = 0, M6 = 1, M7 = -1, M13 = 0. digikit's `sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md` generates one contract from this (classes clobber, keep, stack, never_write). `[doc]` — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#91613fee` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:101](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L101) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. - [doc] Finding 103 was partly withdrawn (2026-11-16): the old assembler mis-encoded several probe instructions, so the silicon run read MMASK as IMASKP, TPERIOD and TCOUNT as I0 and I1, LIRPTL (which SHARC+ lacks) as IMASK, and the cycle-counter reads of records 118-135 as LCNTR reads; it also dropped SSFR's rounding modifier and turned the dual multiply-plus-add into a plain multiply. The values listed in section 6 that came from these items are void; the non-cacheable ranges, REVID, IMASK, MODE2, the 59 value items and the block cycle counts stand (A41). `[doc]` — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#a4254592` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:102](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L102) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / 7. - [doc] Calling convention: a delayed `CALL` with a frame; arguments in R4, R8, R12, more on the stack; result in R0. Most kernels come as a pair: `reset(record)` and `process(record, in, out, n)`, one 32-sample block per call. The prologue and epilogue cost ~20 instructions, about 0.6 per sample. — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#ee7b858d` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:106](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L106) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
- [doc] Every sample loop is a hardware `DO ... UNTIL LCE`. - [doc] Idioms worth copying: multiplier + ALU + data move in one instruction; post-modify DAG access with constant M6 = 1 and M5 = 0; RECIPS/RSQRTS seed plus Newton steps, using FAVG to halve; branch-free CLIP/ABS/MIN/MAX; FEXT to wrap an index; SIMD around copy loops; parameter ramps as "accumulator += step per sample"; MODE1 saved and restored around RND32 or SIMD. — `digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing#4edc108f` [hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md:110](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md#L110) · Digitakt II (OS 1.17) - writing fast and safe SHARC code: lessons from the PLAITS port / What the stock SHARC kernels look like (digikit finding 72, DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12, static)
- [doc] Same code, different address: the shared kernels are byte-identical on DT2 and DN2 but sit at different addresses (biquad DT2 `0x1ccbd8`, DN2 `0xb81368`).
